final.memo:
We find ourselves in a period of extreme financial distress, yet our investment philosophy remains unchanged: we look for wonderful businesses that we can understand, which possess durable competitive advantages and the ability to generate sustainable owner earnings. When others are fearful, the market often provides us with the opportunity to purchase such businesses at prices that offer a substantial margin of safety. While the reported earnings are currently depressed and do not reflect the normalized earning power of these enterprises, the gap between the normalized earnings yield and the 3.99% yield on the long Treasury bond is compelling [D02, D03, D04].

We do not attempt to forecast the bottom of the market or the near-term path of the economy, as such efforts are futile. Instead, we focus on the durability of the underlying businesses and our own liquidity needs. We maintain a strong cash position to ensure we can meet our insurance and contractual obligations, but we are prepared to move decisively when the arithmetic of value favors ownership over fixed-income claims. We remain focused on the long-run distributable cash, indifferent to the temporary volatility captured by the VIX or daily price quotes [D01, D03, D04, D06].
